clue.text: Free at last, we built the foundation of a caring society

definitions.text: the foundation of a caring society

indicators.note: the letters are put together into a new structure, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: At last free, we laid down the groundwork of a compassionate nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' signals that the twelve letters of FREE AT LAST WE are rearranged into one two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of state-funded benefits and healthcare is the base on which a society that looks after its people rests.

clue.text: Punk is dressed by poet in glittering fabric

indicators.note: one piece is clothed by another, so the setter's words sit inside the poet's name

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
Punk is the setter, so from his point of view 'Punk is' becomes 'I am'

explanation.surface: A punk rocker is clothed by a poet in sparkly material.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Punk is' turns into I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamanté is material decorated with sparkling artificial gems or sequins.

clue.text: See 7
Sloppy kiss inspires her local success

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the first pair of pieces takes the other inside

parts.note: sloppy can mean wet, as in sloppy ground
to spoon is an old word for kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: A wet kiss gives a girl the confidence to succeed in her neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is the British word for a neighbourhood pub; Wetherspoon is a very successful UK pub chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub is a local in British slang, and this chain of pubs has been a huge commercial triumph.

clue.text: Fool's written up translation of secular parts for alchemist

indicators.note: the reworked letters separate the two halves of the reversed word, sitting between them
in a down clue, writing upwards means the word runs backwards

parts.note: a sap is a fool; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to what follows

indicators.note: translating something renders it in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool writes a version of some secular passages for a medieval scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses SAP to PAS; RACELSU, rearranged from SECULAR, then 'parts' PA and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracelsus was a sixteenth-century Swiss physician famous as an alchemist.

clue.text: Sultanate where tea is about to be served, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether something was said points to how the words sound when spoken

parts.words: where tea is about to be served
parts.note: brew is tea, and nigh means close at hand, so a brew is nigh

explanation.surface: A question about the country where tea is just about to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei, on Borneo, is ruled by a sultan and so is a sultanate.

clue.text: PM annoyed with the hopeless situation, finally

indicators.note: something hopeless is a mess, so these letters are jumbled
finally points to the closing letter of situation

explanation.surface: A prime minister is irritated by a desperate position at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopeless' signals the rearrangement of ANNOYED, THE and N (the end of 'situation', picked by 'finally').
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony Eden was the British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957, whose term ended with the Suez crisis.

clue.text: Scoundrel I loved is unreliable? Let me think

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be relied on to stay put, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: er is the hesitation noise someone makes while thinking

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the rogue they loved can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who does evil, is a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Unable to produce young nobleman, so to speak?

indicators.note: the phrase points to spoken sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A young aristocrat apparently cannot have children.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren describes a woman or animal that cannot bear offspring; infertile is the synonym.

clue.text: Asian villain having much fun with a criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oriental baddie enjoys himself with a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Fu Manchu is the fictional Chinese master criminal created by Sax Rohmer.

clue.text: Strike consuming a corporation

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so the first word swallows the other

parts.note: to punch is to strike

explanation.surface: Industrial action is eating into a large company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' here is the jocular old word for a big belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a humorous, dated term for a large stomach, a pot belly.

clue.text: Retailer in pain has to verbally express contempt for intimate habits?

indicators.note: spoken words point to how the phrase sounds

parts.note: to boo is to express contempt, and lingerie is intimate clothing (habits being garments)

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper in agony must jeer at someone's private routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' is the French word for bread, so the retailer is a French baker's.
explanation.definitionFit: A French bakery deals in bread, which in French is pain.

clue.text: Approach ladder — one way to go on it?

parts.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

parts.words: one way to go on it
parts.note: on a ladder you can go up (or down)

explanation.surface: How to tackle a ladder: climbing it is one option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' looks like the climbing tool, but it is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper takes, or the period leading to an event.

clue.text: English reserve in political heavyweight, one lacking leadership

parts.note: a portly MP is literally a heavy politician

indicators.note: without its leading letter, the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An English reticence is found in a senior politician who cannot lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Lympne is a wild animal park and nature reserve in Kent, England. 'reserve' wants to mean reticence.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Lympne is a wildlife reserve in Kent, so a nature park in England.

clue.text: Old African went on concealing heroin, as in pants

indicators.note: concealing keeps something hidden inside

parts.note: rode, as on a horse or bus
H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old African carried on hiding drugs, like in his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' signals rearranging AS IN to SIAN; 'pants' as British slang means poor or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhodesian was a native of Rhodesia, the former name of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Destroy sheep munching corn

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so the first piece contains the second

parts.note: a tup is a ram
an ear is the seed head of corn

explanation.surface: Wrecking it: a sheep chomps on maize.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear up a document or plan is to destroy or rip it apart.

clue.text: Dog star, animal in myth

indicators.note: one word placed within another

parts.note: a myth is a falsehood, a lie
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: The star Sirius is an animal in mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog star' wants to be Sirius; here it is a canine film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the collie who starred in films and television, a famous canine celebrity.

clue.text: Lack of movement just north of Chiswick around one

indicators.note: the location phrase goes around the numeral

parts.note: Acton is the London district just north of Chiswick, so in Acton
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: No movement just north of a London suburb, round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiswick and Acton are neighbouring districts of west London, Acton lying just to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a failure to act, an absence of motion or activity.

clue.text: Was obliged to lock me up, when previously guilty

indicators.note: previously puts this piece in front of the rest

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: to lock up is to confine, so the word holds the next inside it
completes the phrase 'lock up', meaning to shut in

parts.note: had, as in 'had to go'

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to imprison me, having earlier been at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling guilty is feeling shame over something done, embarrassed by guilt.

clue.text: Say what made this drinker fat — and hairy?

indicators.note: say asks the solver to speak the words and hear the result

parts.note: the reply to what fattened the drinker is 'beer did'

explanation.surface: A question about what made a fat, hairy drinker so big.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a beard has a hairy face.

clue.text: In America, provincial street keeping shopping centre private

indicators.note: keeping holds something within

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
own, as in one's own room

explanation.surface: An American provincial street has a private shopping centre on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-town is an American term for parochial, narrow-minded or provincial.

clue.text: A playwright reported on land

indicators.note: reported speech points to how the name sounds

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist was said to be on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or to the land, off a ship.

clue.text: See 1
In a doubter, not as sure in conclusion

indicators.note: not removes the following word from the name

parts.note: a doubting Thomas is a sceptic, after the apostle who doubted

indicators.note: the conclusion of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Inside a sceptic, there is less certainty at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the word 'as' from the doubter, as in a doubting Thomas. 'In' is the definition, as in 'staying in' rather than going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being indoors, staying at one's own house.

clue.text: Month before start of refit for vessel

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A month before a ship goes in for a refit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a container for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel into which wine or spirits are poured.

clue.text: A group of musicians on top

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A band is in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, the same as 'on top' when adding something extra.

clue.text: Sovereign, money for job

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch
the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: A gold coin and some cash in payment for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the British gold coin, but it is the monarch, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short task or job, often running to the shops.

clue.text: Great deal spoken about rifle's ultimate pump action?

indicators.note: about turns the pair of words backwards

parts.note: a lot is a great deal
said means spoken

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one of the word

explanation.surface: Much talk about a rifle's final pump-action mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LOT SAID to DIASTOL. 'pump action' suggests a shotgun; the pump is the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle relaxes and fills, part of its pumping cycle.
